question: How is the final overall grade calculated?
expected_answer: Weighted mean of module grades plus the thesis grade, weighted by ECTS; only the first decimal place counts and further digits are dropped without rounding (§ 25 Abs. 2)
actual_answer: ANSWER  The overall grade for the passed Master's examination is calculated as the weighted average of the module grades of compulsory and elective modules, as well as the grade of the Master's thesis and, if applicable, the oral Master's examination and/or the defense of the Master's thesis [D1 § 25 Abs. 2 Sätze 1–7].   The weights are determined by the weights of the associated submodule grades or the allocated ECTS credits. When calculating the final grade, only the first decimal place is considered, and all subsequent decimal places are truncated without rounding [D1 § 25 Abs. 2 Sätze 1–7]. The resulting grade is graded as follows: - up to 1.5: very good (*sehr gut*) - 1.6 to 2.5: good (*gut*) - 2.6 to 3.5: satisfactory (*befriedigend*) - 3.6 to 4.0: sufficient (*ausreichend*) - 4.1 and above: insufficient (*nicht ausreichend*) [D1 § 25 Abs. 2 Sätze 1–7].
